hints: For a geometric distribution $X \sim \text{Geo}(p)$, the expected value is the reciprocal of $p$: $E(X) = 1/p$.
Evaluate $1 / 0.05 = 20$, and explain that 20 is the expected long-run average number of trials up to and including the first success.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the reciprocal formula for the mean of a geometric distribution:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{0.05} = 20 \text{ trials}$$

Interpret the mean in context:
$$\text{Over many repeated runs of the experiment, the mean number of trials required is } 20$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Take the reciprocal of the success probability:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{0.05} = 20$$

State the meaning:
$$\text{It takes on average 20 trials to obtain the first success.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Interprets $20$ as the long-run average number of trials required to achieve the first success.

hints: Use the relation between the mean and success probability: $E(X) = 1/p \implies p = 1/E(X)$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the expectation equation for the unknown parameter $p$:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = 16$$

Rearrange to solve for $p$:
$$p = \frac{1}{16} = 0.0625$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Invert the expected value to find the single-trial probability:
$$p = \frac{1}{16}$$

Write as a fraction or decimal:
$$p = 0.0625$$

hints: Find the probability of rolling a total of 9 with two fair dice: the pairs are $(3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3)$, so $p = 4/36 = 1/9$.
Take the reciprocal of $p$ to find $E(X) = 1 / (1/9) = 9$ throws.

walkthrough.text:
List the ordered pairs giving a sum of 9 on two fair dice:
$$\text{Outcomes: } \{(3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3)\} \implies p = \frac{4}{36} = \frac{1}{9}$$

Calculate the expected number of throws:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{1/9} = 9 \text{ throws}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
There are 4 ways to score 9 out of 36 outcomes:
$$p = \frac{4}{36} = \frac{1}{9}$$

The expected number of rolls is the reciprocal:
$$E(X) = 9$$

hints: Calculate $E(X) = 1 / 0.40 = 2.5$.
Because $X$ only takes integer values, $X > 2.5$ means $X \ge 3$, which is equivalent to $X > 2$. Use $P(X > 2) = q^2 = (0.60)^2 = 0.36$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the expectation:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{0.40} = 2.5$$

Translate the condition $X > 2.5$ for integer values and apply the tail formula:
$$X > 2.5 \iff X \ge 3 \iff X > 2$$
$$P(X > 2) = q^2 = (1 - 0.40)^2 = (0.60)^2 = 0.36$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
More than 2.5 trials means the first two trials must fail:
$$P(X > 2.5) = 0.60^2 = 0.36$$

hints: The success probability is $p = 3/8$, so $E(X) = 1/p = 8/3 = 2\frac{2}{3}$.
The count of spins $X$ must be a whole number, while the mean represents a theoretical long-run average across many trials.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the expectation from $p = 3/8$:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{3/8} = \frac{8}{3} = 2\frac{2}{3} \approx 2.667 \text{ spins}$$

Explain why the mean is not a possible outcome of a single experiment:
$$\text{The random variable } X \text{ takes integer values } X \in \{1, 2, 3, \dots\} \text{; } \frac{8}{3} \text{ is a theoretical long-run average.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Note that no individual run can take a fraction of a spin:
$$\text{You cannot spin } 2\frac{2}{3} \text{ times; the mean is an average across many runs.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that $X$ takes only integer values $\{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$, whereas the mean is a long-run theoretical average.

hints: Use the linearity property of expectation: $E(15 + 5X) = 15 + 5E(X) = 15 + 5(4) = 35$ dollars.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the expected number of trials for $X \sim \text{Geo}(0.25)$:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{0.25} = 4$$

Apply the linearity of expectation to find the expected cost:
$$E(C) = E(15 + 5X) = 15 + 5 E(X) = 15 + 5(4) = 15 + 20 = 35 \text{ dollars}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the expected number of trials:
$$E(X) = 4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies linearity of expectation: $E(C) = 15 + 5 E(X) = 15 + 5(4) = 35$ dollars.

hints: For a geometric distribution, the expectation is $E(X) = 1/p$.
Evaluate $1 / 0.24 = 100 / 24 = 25 / 6 = 4\frac{1}{6}$, and state that this is the long-run average number of attempts.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the mean of the geometric distribution $X \sim \text{Geo}(0.24)$:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{0.24} = \frac{100}{24} = \frac{25}{6} = 4\frac{1}{6} \approx 4.167 \text{ attempts}$$

Provide the contextual interpretation:
$$\text{Over many such candidates, the mean number of attempts taken to pass will approach } \frac{25}{6}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Interpret as a long-run mean:
$$\text{The average number of attempts is } 4\frac{1}{6}\text{; no single candidate takes a fractional attempt.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that $\frac{25}{6}$ represents the theoretical long-run average number of attempts across many candidates.

hints: Fewer than 3 attempts means passing on attempt 1 or attempt 2: $P(X < 3) = P(X \le 2)$.

walkthrough.text:
Translate the strict inequality to a cumulative event:
$$X < 3 \iff X \le 2 \iff 1 - P(X > 2)$$

Calculate using the complement of 2 failures with $q = 0.76$:
$$P(X \le 2) = 1 - q^2 = 1 - (0.76)^2 = 1 - 0.5776 = 0.4224$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Passing on fewer than 3 attempts means within 2 attempts:
$$P(X \le 2) = 1 - 0.76^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Translates fewer than 3 attempts to $P(X < 3) = P(X \le 2) = 1 - (1 - 0.24)^2 = 1 - 0.76^2$.

hints: Use the relationship $E(X) = 1/p \implies p = 1 / E(X)$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the formula relating the mean and parameter $p$:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = 12.5$$

hints: The failure probability is $q = 1 - 0.08 = 0.92$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify failure probability:
$$q = 1 - 0.08 = 0.92$$

Compute $P(X = 5)$ for exact trial 5:
$$P(X = 5) = q^4 p = (0.92)^4 \times 0.08 = 0.71639296 \times 0.08 = 0.05731144 \dots \approx 0.05731 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

Compute $P(X > 8)$ for more than 8 trials:
$$P(X > 8) = q^8 = (0.92)^8 = 0.51321887 \dots \approx 0.5132 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

hints: For $X \sim \text{Geo}(0.16)$, the expected value is $E(X) = 1/p$.
Express the final answer as $6.25$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the reciprocal formula for the mean of $X \sim \text{Geo}(0.16)$:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{0.16}$$

Evaluate the quotient:
$$E(X) = \frac{100}{16} = \frac{25}{4} = 6.25 \text{ turns}$$

hints: Use the linearity of expectation: $E(G) = 100 - 10 E(X) = 100 - 10(6.25) = 37.5$ dollars.
A positive profit means $100 - 10X > 0 \implies 10X < 100 \implies X < 10 \implies X \le 9$.
Evaluate $P(X \le 9) = 1 - (0.84)^9$ and round to 4 significant figures: $0.7918$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the expected net profit using linearity of expectation:
$$E(G) = E(100 - 10X) = 100 - 10 E(X) = 100 - 10(6.25) = 100 - 62.50 = 37.50 \text{ dollars}$$

Determine the condition on $X$ for strictly positive profit:
$$G > 0 \iff 100 - 10X > 0 \iff 10X < 100 \iff X < 10 \iff X \le 9$$
$$\text{where } q = 1 - 0.16 = 0.84$$

Calculate the probability using the cumulative formula:
$$P(X \le 9) = 1 - q^9 = 1 - (0.84)^9 = 1 - 0.20821575 \dots = 0.79178425 \dots \approx 0.7918 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Profit is positive when the contestant wins in 9 or fewer turns:
$$G > 0 \iff X \le 9$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies linearity of expectation: $E(G) = 100 - 10 E(X) = 100 - 10(6.25) = 100 - 62.5 = 37.5$ dollars.

hints: For $p = 0.20$, the expected value is an integer: $E(X) = 1 / 0.20 = 5$.
The tail probability of strictly exceeding 5 is $P(X > 5) = q^5 = (0.80)^5$.
Evaluate $(0.80)^5 = 0.32768$ exactly.

walkthrough.text:
Find the expectation for $p = 0.20$:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{0.20} = 5$$

Set up the tail probability for strictly exceeding the mean:
$$P(X > E(X)) = P(X > 5) = q^5 = (1 - 0.20)^5 = (0.80)^5$$

Evaluate the power:
$$P(X > 5) = (0.80)^5 = 0.32768$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the tail formula for 5 failures:
$$P(X > 5) = 0.80^5$$

hints: Calculate $E(Y) = 1 / 0.35 = 20 / 7 \approx 2.857$.
Because $Y$ takes integer values, $Y > 2.857$ is equivalent to $Y \ge 3$, which is the tail $Y > 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the expectation for $p = 0.35$:
$$E(Y) = \frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{0.35} = \frac{20}{7} \approx 2.8571$$

Translate the condition for integer values:
$$Y > \frac{20}{7} \iff Y \ge 3 \iff Y > 2$$
$$\text{where } q = 1 - 0.35 = 0.65$$

Compute the tail probability:
$$P(Y > 2) = q^2 = (0.65)^2 = 0.4225$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
More than 2.857 trials requires 2 initial failures:
$$P(Y \ge 3) = P(Y > 2) = 0.65^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Translates $Y > \frac{20}{7}$ to integer condition $Y \ge 3 \iff Y > 2$, giving tail $q^2 = (0.65)^2$.

hints: By linearity of expectation, $E(X_A - X_B) = E(X_A) - E(X_B)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the mean number of parts tested for Machine $A$:
$$E(X_A) = \frac{1}{p_A} = \frac{1}{0.05} = 20$$

Calculate the mean number of parts tested for Machine $B$:
$$E(X_B) = \frac{1}{p_B} = \frac{1}{0.08} = 12.5$$

Apply linearity of expectation to find the difference:
$$E(X_A - X_B) = E(X_A) - E(X_B) = 20 - 12.5 = 7.5$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies linearity of expectation: $E(X_A - X_B) = E(X_A) - E(X_B) = 20 - 12.5 = 7.5$.

hints: Set up the threshold inequality: $1 - (0.92)^n > 0.85 \implies (0.92)^n < 0.15$.
Take logarithms: $n > \ln(0.15) / \ln(0.92) \approx 22.753$, so the least integer is $n = 23$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the tail probability $P(X_B > 15)$ for Machine $B$:
$$P(X_B > 15) = q_B^{15} = (0.92)^{15} = 0.28629740 \dots \approx 0.2863 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

Formulate the sample size threshold inequality:
$$1 - (0.92)^n > 0.85 \implies (0.92)^n < 0.15$$
$$n \ln(0.92) < \ln(0.15) \implies n > \frac{\ln(0.15)}{\ln(0.92)} = \frac{-1.897120}{-0.083382} \approx 22.7523$$

Verify with neighbor checks:
$$\text{For } n = 22: \quad 1 - (0.92)^{22} \approx 0.8402 < 0.85$$
$$\text{For } n = 23: \quad 1 - (0.92)^{23} \approx 0.8530 > 0.85 \implies n = 23$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Round up to the next integer:
$$n = 23$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up inequality $1 - (0.92)^n > 0.85 \implies (0.92)^n < 0.15$ and applies logarithms: $n > \frac{\ln(0.15)}{\ln(0.92)} \approx 22.753$.
States least integer $n = 23$ with checks $1 - 0.92^{22} \approx 0.8402 < 0.85$ and $1 - 0.92^{23} \approx 0.8530 > 0.85$.

hints: Rolling double 6 on two fair dice has probability $p = \frac{1}{6} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{36}$.
The expected number of throws for a geometric distribution is the reciprocal of $p$: $E(X) = 1/p = 36$ throws.
For $X = 36$, there are 35 failures followed by 1 success: $(35/36)^{35} \times (1/36)$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the parameter $p$ and the expected waiting time:
$$p = \frac{1}{6} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{36} \implies E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = 36 \text{ throws}$$

Calculate the probability that the double 6 occurs on exactly the 36th throw:
$$P(X = 36) = q^{35} p = \left(\frac{35}{36}\right)^{35}\left(\frac{1}{36}\right) = 0.373073 \times \frac{1}{36} = 0.01036314 \dots \approx 0.01036 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
The expected number of rolls is 36:
$$E(X) = 36$$

Compute 35 non-double-sixes followed by double six:
$$P(X = 36) = \left(\frac{35}{36}\right)^{35}\left(\frac{1}{36}\right) = 0.01036$$

hints: The expected number of throws is $E(X) = 36$.
The tail event $P(X > 36)$ is simply $q^{36} = (35/36)^{36}$.
Evaluate $(35/36)^{36} \approx 0.3627$ (which is close to $1/e \approx 0.3679$).
Round to 4 significant figures: $0.3627$.

walkthrough.text:
Formulate the tail probability of exceeding the mean of 36 throws:
$$P(X > E(X)) = P(X > 36) = q^{36} = \left(\frac{35}{36}\right)^{36}$$

Evaluate using powers:
$$\left(\frac{35}{36}\right)^{36} = \left(1 - \frac{1}{36}\right)^{36} = 0.36271003 \dots \approx 0.3627 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

Note the asymptotic connection:
$$\text{Notice that for large } n, \left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)^n \approx \frac{1}{e} \approx 0.3679$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up the tail for 36 failures:
$$P(X > 36) = \left(\frac{35}{36}\right)^{36}$$

Define the outer binomial model for 4 players: $Y \sim B(4, p_{\text{tail}})$.
At least 2 players means $P(Y \ge 2) = 1 - P(Y = 0) - P(Y = 1)$.

$$P(Y \ge 2) = 1 - P(Y = 0) - P(Y = 1)$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
State the outer binomial model:
$$Y \sim B(4, 0.3627)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Defines outer binomial model $Y \sim B(4, p_{\text{tail}})$ where $p_{\text{tail}} = \left(\frac{35}{36}\right)^{36} \approx 0.362710$ and $P(Y \ge 2) = 1 - P(Y = 0) - P(Y = 1)$.

hints: For $X \sim \text{Geo}(0.08)$, calculate $E(X) = 1/p = 1 / 0.08 = 12.5$ wells.
Apply the linearity of expectation: $E(V) = 40 - 2E(X)$.
Substitute $E(X) = 12.5$ to find $E(V) = 40 - 25 = 15$ million dollars.
State the units clearly.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the expected number of wells drilled:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{0.08} = 12.5 \text{ wells}$$

Use linearity of expectation to find expected net profit $E(V)$:
$$E(V) = E(40 - 2X) = 40 - 2 E(X)$$

Evaluate the profit:
$$E(V) = 40 - 2(12.5) = 40 - 25 = 15 \text{ million dollars}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the expected number of drills:
$$E(X) = \frac{1}{0.08} = 12.5$$

hints: Recall that profit is given by $V = 40 - 2X$.
A financial loss occurs when profit is negative: $40 - 2X < 0 \implies 2X > 40 \implies X > 20$.
The tail probability $P(X > 20)$ is given by $q^{20} = (0.92)^{20}$.
Compute $(0.92)^{20} = 0.188693 \dots$ and round to 4 significant figures: $0.1887$.

walkthrough.text:
Convert the loss condition $V < 0$ into an inequality for $X$:
$$V < 0 \iff 40 - 2X < 0 \iff 2X > 40 \iff X > 20$$
$$\text{where } q = 1 - 0.08 = 0.92$$

Apply the tail formula for strictly more than 20 wells:
$$P(X > 20) = q^{20} = (0.92)^{20}$$

Evaluate to 4 significant figures:
$$P(X > 20) = 0.18869333 \dots \approx 0.1887 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Loss occurs if more than 20 wells are drilled:
$$V < 0 \iff X > 20$$

hints: The project is abandoned if all 15 wells fail: $P(X > 15) = (0.92)^{15} \approx 0.2863$.
For the threshold, set $1 - (0.92)^M \ge 0.90 \implies (0.92)^M \le 0.10$.
Solve using logarithms: $M \ge \ln(0.10) / \ln(0.92) \approx 27.615$.
Conclude that the least integer number of wells is $M = 28$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability that the project is abandoned after 15 failures:
$$P(\text{abandoned}) = P(X > 15) = q^{15} = (0.92)^{15} = 0.28629740 \dots \approx 0.2863 \text{ (4 s.f.)}$$

Formulate the sample size inequality for a $90\%$ success target:
$$1 - (0.92)^M \ge 0.90 \implies (0.92)^M \le 0.10$$
$$M \ln(0.92) \le \ln(0.10) \implies M \ge \frac{\ln(0.10)}{\ln(0.92)} = \frac{-2.302585}{-0.083382} \approx 27.6150$$

Confirm the integer with neighbor checks:
$$\text{For } M = 27: \quad 1 - (0.92)^{27} \approx 0.8951 < 0.90$$
$$\text{For } M = 28: \quad 1 - (0.92)^{28} \approx 0.9035 \ge 0.90 \implies M = 28$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the chance of 15 consecutive dry wells:
$$P(X > 15) = 0.92^{15} = 0.2863$$

Round up to the nearest integer:
$$M = 28$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up threshold inequality $1 - (0.92)^M \ge 0.90 \implies (0.92)^M \le 0.10$ and takes logarithms: $M \ge \frac{\ln(0.10)}{\ln(0.92)} \approx 27.615$.
States least integer $M = 28$ with checks $1 - 0.92^{27} \approx 0.8951 < 0.90$ and $1 - 0.92^{28} \approx 0.9035 > 0.90$.
